title: Invertibility and monoidal coherence of the normalized exact derived tensor comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with their fixed K-flat derived tensor structures [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Flat means that tensoring on either side preserves short exact sequences; K-flat complexes and the signed direct-sum total tensor are as in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso].
Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive exact left adjoint with a specified strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], preserving flat objects and K-flat complexes. Write $F_{\rm Ch}$ for its termwise functor and $\tau_{P,Q}:F_{\rm Ch}(P\otimes Q)\cong F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes F_{\rm Ch}Q$ for the direct-sum total comparison induced by the inverse ordinary tensorator. Put $E=D(F)$, let $Q_{\mathcal C},Q_{\mathcal D}$ be localization from complexes, and let $\kappa_P:E Q_{\mathcal C}P\cong Q_{\mathcal D}F_{\rm Ch}P$ be the canonical exact-functor factorization.
Let $m_{\mathcal C;P,Q}:Q_{\mathcal C}(P\otimes Q)\cong Q_{\mathcal C}P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_{\mathcal C}Q$ and $m_{\mathcal D}$ be the native K-flat model comparisons. Let $t:E(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)\to EK\otimes^{\mathbf L}EL$ be the natural comparison of [lem-pur-derived-tensor-comparison], normalized for every K-flat pair $P,Q$ by
$$(\kappa_P\otimes\kappa_Q)\circ t_{Q_{\mathcal C}P,Q_{\mathcal C}Q}\circ E(m_{\mathcal C;P,Q})=m_{\mathcal D;FP,FQ}\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{P,Q})\circ\kappa_{P\otimes Q}.$$
Write $u_{\mathcal C}:Q_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}[0])\cong\mathbf1_{D(\mathcal C)}$ and $u_{\mathcal D}$ for the native unit models, and $e_F:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\cong F\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ for the ordinary unit map. Define
$$e=u_{\mathcal D}\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(e_F^{-1}[0])\circ\kappa_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}[0]}\circ E(u_{\mathcal C}^{-1}).$$
Then every $t_{K,L}$ is invertible and, for all $K,L,M$, the native derived associator $\alpha$ and unitors $\lambda,\rho$ satisfy
$$(1\otimes t_{L,M})\circ t_{K,L\otimes^{\mathbf L}M}\circ E(\alpha_{K,L,M})=\alpha_{EK,EL,EM}\circ(t_{K,L}\otimes1)\circ t_{K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L,M},$$
$$E(\lambda_K)=\lambda_{EK}\circ(e\otimes1)\circ t_{\mathbf1,K},\qquad E(\rho_K)=\rho_{EK}\circ(1\otimes e)\circ t_{K,\mathbf1}.$$
Thus $t^{-1},e^{-1}$ give a strong monoidal structure on $E$ with exactly these normalized maps. No compatibility of $F$ with a braiding is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived). Agent extraction of cross-functor normalization for the K-flat structures; the abstract exact-functor assertion is not a verbatim Stacks theorem.

proof.text: Both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], so all small colimits exist in them. Use [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] for $F$ and for tensoring with a fixed object: closedness gives the right adjoint to left tensor, and symmetry conjugates right tensor to left tensor. Thus $F$ preserves the countable coproducts, and the tensor functors preserve the colimits, required by [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal]. Apply that statement to the specified ordinary structure of $F$. It gives exactly the comparison $\tau$ of the item (its summand formula specifies it uniquely), the map $j=e_F^{-1}[0]$, and their associativity and both unit equations on unbounded complexes. We will use these three equations, without a braiding equation.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); explicit agent proof of the abstract cross-functor normalization

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution], every complex $A$ admits a K-flat quasi-isomorphism $P\to A$; all its hypotheses are the stated Grothendieck, closed symmetric monoidal and functorial-flat-resolution hypotheses. Hence every derived object is isomorphic to $Q_{\mathcal C}P$ with $P$ K-flat. The unit complex $I=\mathbf1[0]$ is K-flat: its two tensor functors are naturally the identity by the complex unitors. K-flat objects are closed under tensor: for a quasi-isomorphism $s$, reassociation identifies $(P\otimes Q)\otimes s$ with $P\otimes(Q\otimes s)$, a composite application of two quasi-isomorphism-preserving functors; on the other side use $s\otimes(P\otimes Q)\cong(s\otimes P)\otimes Q$. These use exactly the two-sided definition in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] and the complex associator of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. By the hypothesis on $F$, all $FP,FQ,F(P\otimes Q),FI$ appearing below are K-flat too.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); explicit agent proof of the abstract cross-functor normalization

proof.text:
For a K-flat pair the stated normalization solves for the comparison:
$$t_{Q_{\mathcal C}P,Q_{\mathcal C}Q}=(\kappa_P\otimes\kappa_Q)^{-1}\circ m_{\mathcal D;FP,FQ}\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{P,Q})\circ\kappa_{P\otimes Q}\circ E(m_{\mathcal C;P,Q})^{-1}.$$
Every factor is an isomorphism: the $m$'s are the native K-flat model comparisons, the $\kappa$'s are the given factorization isomorphisms, and Step 1 gives $\tau$. Thus $t$ is invertible on K-flat model pairs. Likewise the formula defining $e$ is a composite of isomorphisms, so $e$ is invertible. No resolution of the unit is needed since Step 2 shows $I$ is K-flat.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); explicit agent proof of the abstract cross-functor normalization

proof.text:
Here are the native constraint equations used in the remaining calculations. For either coefficient category $\mathcal A$, abbreviate its localization to $q$, and define, for K-flat $P,Q,R$,
$$A_{\mathcal A}^l=(m_{P,Q}\otimes1)\circ m_{P\otimes Q,R},\qquad A_{\mathcal A}^r=(1\otimes m_{Q,R})\circ m_{P,Q\otimes R}.$$
The assertion in [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] that the constraints are induced from complexes and localization is lax monoidal gives
$$\alpha^{D(\mathcal A)}\circ A_{\mathcal A}^l=A_{\mathcal A}^r\circ q(\alpha^{\rm Ch}),$$
$$\lambda^{D(\mathcal A)}_{qP}\circ(u_{\mathcal A}\otimes1)\circ m_{I,P}=q(\lambda^{\rm Ch}_P),\qquad\rho^{D(\mathcal A)}_{qP}\circ(1\otimes u_{\mathcal A})\circ m_{P,I}=q(\rho^{\rm Ch}_P).$$
Explicitly these are the associativity and unit coherence equations of its lax tensorator $m^{-1}$, multiplied by the indicated invertible $m$'s and by the unit comparison. The complex constraints here are the actual ones of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy], not constraints transported along $F$.

proof.text:
Check associativity at $K=Q_{\mathcal C}P,L=Q_{\mathcal C}Q,M=Q_{\mathcal C}R$. Let $T=(P\otimes Q)\otimes R$. Precompose each proposed side with $E(A_{\mathcal C}^l)$ and postcompose with $\kappa_P\otimes(\kappa_Q\otimes\kappa_R)$. Substitute the normalization twice in each side. Naturality of $t$ moves $m_{P,Q}$ or $m_{Q,R}$ across its outer occurrence, and naturality of $\kappa$ replaces $E(Q_{\mathcal C}a)$ by $Q_{\mathcal D}(Fa)$ conjugated by $\kappa$. Step 4 moves the native associators. The resulting left and right composites are, respectively,
$$A_{\mathcal D}^r\circ Q_{\mathcal D}((1\otimes\tau_{Q,R})\circ\tau_{P,Q\otimes R}\circ F_{\rm Ch}(\alpha^{\rm Ch}))\circ\kappa_T,$$
$$A_{\mathcal D}^r\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(\alpha^{\rm Ch}\circ(\tau_{P,Q}\otimes1)\circ\tau_{P\otimes Q,R})\circ\kappa_T,$$
where $A_{\mathcal D}^r$ is evaluated at $FP,FQ,FR$. Their inner maps agree by [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal]. Step 2 makes every model comparison used here invertible, including those for the intermediate tensor complexes. Cancel the common pre- and postcomposition isomorphisms to obtain exactly the asserted derived associativity equation on this triple.

proof.text:
For the left unit at $K=Q_{\mathcal C}P$, put $B_l=(u_{\mathcal C}\otimes1)\circ m_{\mathcal C;I,P}$. By Step 4, $\lambda_K\circ B_l=Q_{\mathcal C}(\lambda_P^{\rm Ch})$. Thus precomposing $E(\lambda_K)$ with $E(B_l)$ and postcomposing with $\kappa_P$ gives
$$Q_{\mathcal D}(F_{\rm Ch}(\lambda_P^{\rm Ch}))\circ\kappa_{I\otimes P}.$$
For the other side, naturality of $t$ moves $E(u_{\mathcal C}\otimes1)$ to $E(u_{\mathcal C})\otimes1$; its product with $e$ is explicitly
$$e\circ E(u_{\mathcal C})=u_{\mathcal D}\circ Q_{\mathcal D}(j)\circ\kappa_I.$$
The normalization at $(I,P)$ now replaces $(\kappa_I\otimes\kappa_P)tE(m_{I,P})$ by $m_{FI,FP}Q_{\mathcal D}(\tau_{I,P})\kappa_{I\otimes P}$. Naturality of $m$ with respect to $j:FI\cong I_{\mathcal D}$ and Step 4's left-unitor equation give for the second composite
$$Q_{\mathcal D}(\lambda_{FP}^{\rm Ch}\circ(j\otimes1)\circ\tau_{I,P})\circ\kappa_{I\otimes P}.$$
This equals the first composite by the left-unit identity of [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal]. Cancel $E(B_l)$ and $\kappa_P$, both isomorphisms. This proves the stated left-unit equation with precisely the defined $e$.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); explicit agent proof of the abstract cross-functor normalization

proof.text:
For the right unit put $B_r=(1\otimes u_{\mathcal C})\circ m_{\mathcal C;P,I}$. Step 4 gives $\rho_KB_r=Q_{\mathcal C}(\rho_P^{\rm Ch})$. Precompose both sides of the proposed right-unit identity by $E(B_r)$ and postcompose by $\kappa_P$. The first becomes
$$Q_{\mathcal D}(F_{\rm Ch}(\rho_P^{\rm Ch}))\circ\kappa_{P\otimes I}.$$
For the second, naturality of $t$ in its second variable introduces $E(u_{\mathcal C})$ next to $e$. Insert the displayed formula for $eE(u_{\mathcal C})$ from Step 6, then the normalization at $(P,I)$. Naturality of $m$ for $1\otimes j$ and Step 4's right-unitor equation reduce it to
$$Q_{\mathcal D}(\rho_{FP}^{\rm Ch}\circ(1\otimes j)\circ\tau_{P,I})\circ\kappa_{P\otimes I}.$$
These are equal by the right-unit identity of [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal]. Cancellation of $E(B_r)$ and $\kappa_P$ proves the right-unit assertion on $K=Q_{\mathcal C}P$.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); explicit agent proof of the abstract cross-functor normalization

proof.text:
Choose model isomorphisms $a:Q_{\mathcal C}P\cong K$, $b:Q_{\mathcal C}Q\cong L$, $c:Q_{\mathcal C}R\cong M$ as in Step 2. Naturality gives
$$t_{K,L}= (Ea\otimes Eb)\circ t_{QP,QQ}\circ E(a\otimes b)^{-1},$$
so every $t_{K,L}$ is invertible by Step 3. For associativity, precompose the two sides by $E((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and postcompose by $(Ea\otimes(Eb\otimes Ec))^{-1}$. Naturality of $t$ and $\alpha$ makes them the two model composites of Step 5; cancel these isomorphisms. For the left and right unit equations precompose by $E(1\otimes a)$ and $E(a\otimes1)$ respectively and postcompose by $(Ea)^{-1}$: naturality of $t,\lambda,\rho$ gives exactly Steps 6 and 7. Hence all three identities hold at arbitrary unbounded objects.

source.place: Tags 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); explicit agent proof of the abstract cross-functor normalization

proof.text:
Set $\mu_{K,L}=t_{K,L}^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon=e^{-1}$. Inverting the isomorphisms in the three proved equations, or multiplying each equation by its two tensor-comparison inverses and by $e^{-1}$ in the unit cases, gives
$$E(\alpha)\mu_{K\otimes L,M}(\mu_{K,L}\otimes1)=\mu_{K,L\otimes M}(1\otimes\mu_{L,M})\alpha,$$
$$E(\lambda_K)\mu_{\mathbf1,K}(\varepsilon\otimes1)=\lambda_{EK},\qquad E(\rho_K)\mu_{K,\mathbf1}(1\otimes\varepsilon)=\rho_{EK}.$$
Together with the inverse of the naturality equation for $t$, these are precisely the definition [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. This gives the requested structure with the prescribed maps.
